config.title: Margin Collapse

intro.title: Margin Collapse
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with stacked paragraphs to visually explore how margin collapse works in CSS. You will learn the core concept that when vertical margins of adjacent elements touch, they combine into a single margin instead of adding together. The main technologies involved are CSS margin properties and the box model. By adjusting margins on different elements, you'll see how this behavior affects spacing and layout. This foundational knowledge will help you predict and control spacing in your web designs more effectively.
intro.usecase: Margin collapse is a crucial CSS concept that developers encounter daily when building consistent spacing in real-world interfaces. You'll see it in action when creating navigation menus where list items need consistent vertical spacing, in dashboard cards that stack neatly without excessive gaps, or in article layouts where paragraphs and headings should have predictable spacing. Understanding margin collapse helps you avoid unexpected spacing issues in forms, modals, and content panels, ensuring your UI elements align perfectly without manual adjustments.

objectives: Apply margin collapse principles to adjacent vertical elements
Construct layouts that demonstrate collapsing versus non-collapsing margins
Manipulate margin values to control spacing between collapsed elements
Configure parent-child relationships to prevent unwanted margin collapse
Implement clear separation between collapsed and non-collapsed margin scenarios
Control vertical spacing efficiency using margin collapse behavior
Initialize margin values that demonstrate different collapse outcomes

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with two adjacent divs
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with two adjacent div elements inside a container div. Use the class names 'container', 'box1', and 'box2' for the elements.
steps.hint: Start with a container div that wraps two separate div elements placed one after another.

steps.title: Add basic styling to visualize the divs
steps.instruction: Inside the <style> tag, add CSS rules to give both .box1 and .box2 a background color, height, and width so they become visible boxes.
steps.hint: You can use properties like background-color, height, and width. For example, set background-color to a color like lightblue, height to 100px, and width to 200px.

steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but ensure both .box1 and .box2 have background-color, height, and width defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added rules for .box1 and .box2 with background-color, height, and width inside the <style> tag.

steps.instruction: In the CSS, add a margin-top property to the .box1 selector to create space above the first box.
steps.hint: Use the margin-top property with a value like 30px or 2em.

steps.title: Observe margin collapse between adjacent elements
steps.instruction: Inspect the rendered page and notice that the space between the two boxes is determined by the larger of the two adjacent margins, not their sum.
steps.hint: Look at the visual spacing between Box 1 and Box 2. The margins are collapsing vertically.

/* When two elements have adjacent vertical margins, the larger margin wins */
/* Example: margin-top: 20px and margin-bottom: 30px collapse to 30px */

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Add a border property to the .box1 CSS rule to give it a visible border.

Box 1

steps.expectedOutcome: The first div (.box1) will have a visible border, which will prevent its bottom margin from collapsing with the top margin of the second div.
successCriteria: The .box1 CSS rule includes a border property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a border property to the .box1 rule. Check that it's inside the curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: It looks like the border wasn't added correctly. Ensure you add a border property (like 'border: 1px solid black;') to the .box1 CSS rule.

steps.title: Create nested elements to demonstrate parent-child margin collapse
steps.instruction: Add a new parent div with a child div inside the existing container, and apply a top margin to the parent to observe parent-child margin collapse.
steps.hint: Add a new div element with a class like 'parent' inside the container, then add a child div inside it with a class like 'child'. Apply margin-top to the parent div.

steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML structure now includes a parent div with a child div inside, and the parent has a top margin applied to demonstrate parent-child margin collapse.
successCriteria: A parent div with a class (e.g., 'parent') containing a child div with a class (e.g., 'child') is added inside the container, and the parent has margin-top defined in the CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add padding to parent to prevent parent-child margin collapse
steps.instruction: Add a padding-top property to the parent container to separate the child's margin from the parent's margin.
steps.hint: Add 'padding-top: 1px;' to the .container selector in your CSS.
